answer: Hardware-bound quotas. A summit sensor, oasis monitor, or network vertex gets one reward slot per epoch for each certified secure chip. The verifier checks a fresh signed nonce and the chip's fixed manufacturer-certified identifier, merging all accounts that present the same identifier. N slots require N physical chips, so an attacker bears their purchase or rental cost; extra keys on one chip add no quota. This assumes certificates bind to non-clonable hardware and issuers do not certify virtual chips; leaked attestation keys break the limit.
